simple.meaning: עַיִט (ʻayiṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a hawk or other bird of prey.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Genesis, Job, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Genesis 15:11. Its contexts include mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַיִט (H5861).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: a hawk or other bird of prey
definitions.full: H5861. ayit עַ֫יִט noun masculine Jer 12:19 bird(s) of prey (from scream ); — absolute ׳ע Gen 15:11 +, עָ֑יִט Job 28:7 , with article (perhaps) ׳הַע Jer 12:9 b (compare Gie; ׳הַע interrogative v a ); construct עֵיט Isa 18:6 ; Ezek 39:4 ; — usually collective Gen 15:11 (JE), Isa 18:6 ; Job 28:7 , הָרִים עֵיט Isa 18:6 , כָּלכָּֿנָף צִמּוֺר עֵיט Ezek 39:4 ; figurative of foes of Judah Jer 12:9 b; of single bird 12:9 a (figurative of Judah), Isa 46:11 (figurative of invader, || עֲצָתִי אִישׁ ).

occurrences.englishText: The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
That path no bird of prey knows,

They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will eat them in the summer, and all the animals of the earth will eat them in the winter.

I call a ravenous bird from the east,
Is my heritage to me as a speckled bird of prey?

You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you, and all your hordes, and the peoples who are with you. I will give you to the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the animals of the field to be devoured.
